items.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

ctx.x: Well Joe was my good friend and we played together — I did his last album. Joe and I belonged to an organization together that we spent time together. And Bushkin used to — he told me, he says, “Fred, you were born too late.” And of course Bushkin, you know who Bushkin’s best friend was Bunny Berigan. That was his buddy. He says, “I love Harry James, believe me,” he says, “but nobody played like Bunny. He was the best you know. And oh Bushkin was something else. But let me digress for a second about Corky…

a key to the union, I can go down there and anytime and jam anytime I want, why don’t you guys come down and jam with me?” So he keeps bugging the piano player. So 2:00 in the morning, whatever, they go down to the union. He says, “Okay, kid, what do you want to play?” “Well play ‘Cherokee.’” And that was the tune. Okay. “What key do you want to do it in?” “All of them. We’ll start with C and go around the horn.” “Really? What tempo?” “Well about [beats rhythm]” So he gets done playing, “Can you play a ballad?”…
That’s sort of like a basketball team. Like you’ve been traded man.
